items.summary: 02.01.01 rendered the contested badge on the work's ledger 'for all who can see the work', while the canonical rule — 02.01.02 D-06, ratified as the authoritative reconciliation and explicitly resolving the suppression/marker question 02.01.01 deferred to it — scopes the contested marker to participants and the credited party, never the public. Fixed 02.01.01's four drifted restatements (Fan Role Lens, two edge-case rows, the Contested lifecycle row) to state the canonical scope, and appended a pointer to D-11's rationale distinguishing what D-11 owns (mark, never suppress) from what D-06 owns (who the mark renders to). Added Q-07 for the one genuinely open sub-question: the membership of 'participant' on a multi-session work ledger.
items.canonicalSource: 02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.02-public-discography.md:154 (D-06) — "**A contest is not published.** A contested credit stays on the public page at its existing derived tier with no public marker; the contested marker is a record-view affordance for participants and the credited party." Reinforced by the same file:137 — "The single winning rule, stated once: contest = a public marker on the record view for participants only; the public discography line is unchanged and never hidden" — and by credits-attribution-cx.md:297 (CX-16 synthesis Q3) — "only participants see the contested marker". 02.01.02:126 records that 02.01.01 explicitly deferred this behavior: "this pass resolves a behavior `02.01.01` explicitly deferred here: its Contested edge case left the discography suppression rules open for Step 5 to settle. Answered by D-06."

edits.before: They also never see the ledger's internals: no assertion gap, no asserter identity, no origin, or owner-only comp-out trigger date/reason.
edits.after: They also never see the ledger's internals: no assertion gap, no asserter identity, no origin, no **contested state** (`02.01.02` D-06; CX-16 — a contest is participant-and-credited-party record-view information, so the line renders unmarked at its existing derived tier), or owner-only comp-out trigger date/reason.
edits.rationale: The Fan is the exact viewer the contradiction produced two different pages for. Matches 02.01.02:23's Fan lens verbatim in substance.

edits.location: Edge Cases — 'Party disputes a record naming them'
edits.before: User Sees column read: 'Contested badge on the work's ledger for all who can see the work.'
edits.after: What Happens column now states the marker is participant-and-credited-party record-view information, never a public disclosure, and that the viewer-scoped ledger renders the line unchanged at its existing derived tier for non-participants (citing 02.01.02 D-06; credits-attribution CX-16). User Sees column now reads: 'Participants and the credited party: contested badge on the record view within the work's ledger. Everyone else: the same line, unmarked. On the disputing party's own discography: gone, if they set it Private'.
edits.rationale: This is the cell that published pendency to the public — the harm 02.01.02 DT-05 calls 'the most consequential finding in this pass'. Column count preserved (3 columns).

edits.location: Edge Cases — 'A contest is filed to censor a true credit'
edits.before: User Sees column read: 'Contested badge — visible, not absent'
edits.after: What Happens column gains '— and it marks only for participants and the credited party, because publishing pendency is the mirror-image weapon (`02.01.02` D-06/DT-05)'. User Sees column now reads: 'Record still there — visible, not absent. Badge to participants and the credited party only'.
edits.rationale: The row's point is that the *record* is not suppressed, which D-11 owns and is unchanged. Only the badge's audience was wrong. Naming the mirror-image weapon keeps the two halves of the rule legible together. Column count preserved (3 columns).

edits.before: Contested marker on the work's ledger; zero weight in derived surfaces; downstream royalty/reputation effects held
edits.after: Contested marker on the work's ledger **for participants and the credited party only** (`02.01.02` D-06; CX-16) — every other viewer sees the line unchanged at its existing derived tier; zero weight in derived surfaces; downstream royalty/reputation effects held
edits.rationale: Unscoped restatement of the same rule; brought in line. Column count preserved (3 columns).

edits.location: Decisions — D-11 rationale column (decision statement untouched)
edits.before: Rationale ended: '... Two controls, no weapon.'
edits.after: Rationale gains: '**Who the mark is rendered to** is the companion question this feature deferred to `02.01.02`, answered there by D-06: participants and the credited party, on the record view, never the public — this ledger is viewer-scoped, so the two halves compose (mark without suppressing, mark without publishing).'
edits.rationale: D-11's statement — 'Contest marks; it never suppresses' — is canonical for suppression and was NOT changed. It is silent on marker audience, and 02.01.02:126 records that 02.01.01 deferred that question. The addition is a pointer, not a new rule, and prevents the next reader from re-deriving the drift from a decision that looks complete.

edits.after: | Q-07 | **Who is a "participant" for the contested-marker audience?** ... every party holding a credit on the work, only the parties on the captured session the disputed record came from, or only the parties to the dispute case itself. The three sets diverge on a multi-session work: a mixing engineer who never met the tracking drummer would see, or not see, that the drummer's credit is under objection. Scoping under a ratified rule, not a new rule. | Agent | `/write-architecture-spec` (02.01 shard) |
edits.rationale: The ratified rule fixes the public/non-public boundary but no file in the tree defines 'participant' set membership on a work ledger (as opposed to a session). Owner: Agent — it is scoping under a settled rule, not a product decision. Deferral target: /write-architecture-spec, the 02.01 shard, which must express the read-scope predicate. Table column count preserved (4 columns).

items.consistencyCheck: Swept all 12 md files in the domain for contest/marker/ledger/public co-occurrence. 02.01.02 (D-06, DT-05, line 137), 02.01.05:161, 02.03.02:62, 02.03.03:43/44/52/66/76/105, 02.04.02:144, 02.05:21/36/56/69/70/95, and credits-attribution-cx.md CX-16 all already state the participant-only rule. 02.01.01 was the sole holdout — 02.01.02's reconciliation corrected 02.05 D-02 and 02.03.03 D-03 but never swept back into 02.01.01. No file outside the shard required a change. No remaining occurrence of 'for all who can see the work'.
